text:
alice: Quick brain-dump — thinking about switching to coarse-grained 'queue epochs' to reduce lock contention in the continuous batcher. TL;DR: group enqueue/dequeue decisions into epochs (5–20ms) so we make fewer global scheduling decisions. Tradeoff: slight P50 increase for simpler admission and much lower P99 jitter. Thoughts?
ben: Nice sketch. My main worry is small/request fastpath latency — microbursts could get hit badly by a 10–20ms epoch.
carla: We tried something vaguely similar in prefetch land. Biggest pain was headroom signaling granularity. If epochs are too long preemption is slow and you see queuing amplification.
david: Do we plan epoch alignment across workers or per-worker epochs? Global tick seems expensive.
eva: @david leaning to per-worker epochs + a low-cost watermark sync. Rough config idea:
```json
{
  "epoch_ms": 10,
  "max_hold_ms": 30,
  "alignment": "per_worker",
  "min_fastpath_tokens": 8,
  "admission_window_ms": 4
}
```
Optimization: allow micro-fastpath bypass when (tokens <= min_fastpath_tokens).
ben: How do we handle KV-cache lifecycle? Holding requests until epoch end could increase cache pressure and pin entries longer.
alice: Good call. Plan: mark allocs as 'releaseable' at epoch boundary and run staggered async evictions so we avoid bursty cache churn. Also support a soft-preempt hint so very long requests can be split across epochs.
scheduler-bot: [metric-sim] epoch_ms=15 -> simulated P50 +6ms, P99 -10ms compared to no-epoch baseline (workload: mixed chat + embeddings).
carla: Also fairness: if one tenant spikes it can monopolize an epoch. Need per-tenant credits or slice epochs by tenant until we have better isolation.
david: Admission suggestion: at epoch start compute expected batch size and accept only if headroom >= min_tokens_for_batch; otherwise route to dedicated fastpath or immediate reject. Keeps SLOs predictable.
eva: Risk for streaming: token-at-a-time flows may suffer if we batch admission. Suggest hybrid: use epochs for allocation/admission but once started allow streaming to emit tokens as they arrive. That keeps interactive feel.
ben: :thumbsup: I'll prototype on a tiny cluster: epoch_ms=8 and fastpath fallback enabled. Want an A/B test against current continuous-batcher.
alice: I'll draft RFC follow-up with API deltas: new BatcherConfig.{epoch_mode, epoch_ms, fastpath_threshold, eviction_stagger_ms} + telemetry (epoch_wait_ms histogram, epoch_queue_length). Minimal public API change: none for callers, purely scheduler config. Posting draft tomorrow.
carla: Add an e2e test that simulates a noisy tenant with small steady requests + one large burst. We need to surface per-epoch fairness regressions.
david: Also add a chaos test for clock skew between workers — per-worker epochs + watermark resync should be robust but worth validating.
eva: Cool. If prototype looks good we can roll canary behind a feature flag per-pool.
alice: Great — assign owners: ben -> prototype, alice -> RFC + telemetry schema, carla -> e2e fairness tests, david -> chaos clock-skew tests. I'll add a short checklist in the RFC. :sparkles:
